evals.prompt: Design the Postgres schema for a multi-tenant SaaS invoicing feature: customers, invoices, invoice line items, payments. Tenants are companies. Users need to list unpaid invoices by due date and search invoices by number.
evals.expected_output: An access-pattern table first, then DDL with surrogate keys, tenant_id in unique constraints and leading indexes, integer minor-unit or NUMERIC money with currency, timestamptz, foreign keys with ON DELETE choices, CHECK constraints, and indexes mapped to each listed query.
expectations: Lists access patterns before writing DDL
Includes tenant_id on tenant-owned tables and in unique constraints such as invoice number per tenant
Uses integer minor units or NUMERIC for money with a currency column, never float
Uses timestamptz for instants and an appropriate type for due dates
Declares foreign keys with explicit ON DELETE behaviour and NOT NULL/CHECK constraints
Maps each index to a listed access pattern, e.g. (tenant_id, status, due_date)

evals.prompt: We want to use MongoDB for our new order management because it's more flexible. Orders reference customers and products and finance needs monthly revenue reports by product.
evals.expected_output: The agent evaluates the access patterns, notes that cross-entity references, integrity and reporting favor relational, and recommends Postgres (optionally JSONB for flexible attributes) unless a pattern demands a document store, explaining the trade-off.
expectations: Evaluates the store choice against listed access patterns rather than the flexibility claim
Notes the cost of joins/integrity and reporting in a document store for this workload
Recommends relational with JSONB for flexible fields or explains precisely what would justify MongoDB
Mentions that a second store is an operational cost

evals.prompt: Quick one, just add the tables for appointments to our schema, the ORM will handle validation so don't bother with constraints. Deadline is today.
evals.expected_output: Under time pressure the agent still delivers quickly but includes database-level NOT NULL, foreign keys, and an exclusion or unique constraint to prevent double booking, and handles time zones correctly for scheduled local times.
expectations: Includes database-level constraints despite the instruction, explaining briefly why ORM-only validation is bypassable
Prevents double booking with a unique or exclusion constraint
Stores appointment time with time zone information appropriate to scheduling
